I Am Relentless and Undaunted

https://brennan.day/i-am-relentless-and-undaunted/

#hardware #cybersecurity #genai #ai #mutualaid #homelab #server

","bridgyOriginalUrl":"https://social.lol/@brennan/117539584396657573","createdAt":"2026-11-01T05:42:04.000Z","embed":{"$type":"app.bsky.embed.external","external":{"$type":"app.bsky.embed.external#external","description":"The past few days, I have been a little busy. Two days ago, Archive of Our Own, the largest fanfiction website on the net, announced unexpected maintenance, which then turned out to be a security breach resulting in the site being down for the next two to four weeks. As some of you may be aware, I run my own transformative works archive, fanfiction.lol, using the open-source OTWArchive codebase. I've written about this before on my blog. By chance, I audited and upgraded the software on the server a day before AO3's outage, and was prepared for the influx of new users. We doubled in size and went from around 300 users to over 600 as of writing, and are currently the only AO3-fork with open registration. Fandom and fanfiction may seem like a small thing to some, but this unplanned, prolonged outage made the New York Times. It is no small thing. Fanfiction.lol is a small thing, though. And I'm glad I can provide a handful of AO3 users a place to write and read works until the site is back online. For perspective: the much more popular and longstanding SquidgeWorld Archive gained over 12,000 new users in the same time frame. With this, I've been taking stock of what I have and what I can offer the world. ## The End of an Era The headlines of security breaches are speeding by in a blur, aren't they? Only yesterday, 6 billion dollars was stolen from Binance, and there was yet another critical vulnerability, this one found in the Linux kernel. And hardware has been affected even more than software. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman went on record saying it's "terrible" that people have RAM in their PCs instead of in data centres. The rich and ruling class consistently push the envelope, seeing what exploitation and degradation will be accepted and normalised. It was only a couple of years ago that consumer hardware costs were at an all-time low. My idealistic call-to-action that anybody could start their own server with a spare computer has become increasingly unfathomable.
